title: Best Dog Cooling Mats 2026: Green Pet Shop vs K&H vs Chillz
description: Five dog cooling mats compared on cooling type (pressure-activated gel vs water), durability against chewing, size, and price — from the budget Chillz to the popular Green Pet Shop gel mat.
lede: A dog cooling mat can be a genuine relief for an overheating dog in summer — but only the right kind, used the right way. The split nobody explains is between self-cooling gel mats (no power, no water) and water-filled mats, and a chewer can destroy either in an afternoon if you pick wrong.

sections.heading: Top pick: The Green Pet Shop Cooling Mat
paragraphs: The Green Pet Shop Cooling Mat is the best dog cooling mat for most owners because it uses convenient pressure-activated gel cooling that needs no electricity, no water, and no refrigeration — it works the moment your dog lies on it. Inside is a non-toxic cooling gel that activates under the dog's weight, drawing heat away from the body to keep the dog cooler for a stretch before it needs a short period without pressure to recharge (the gel re-cools itself automatically once the dog steps off for a while). You simply lay it on the floor, in a crate, on a bed, or in the car, and it works — no plugging in, no filling, no freezer space.

Its appeal is exactly that no-fuss self-cooling convenience plus a proven track record: it's one of the most popular and recommended cooling mats precisely because the pressure-activated gel genuinely works without any setup, it comes in multiple sizes for different dogs, it folds for travel, and it's durable and wipeable. For a dog that overheats in summer, settles on hard floors, or needs cooling in a crate or car, it's the easy, reliable choice that requires nothing but laying it down.

The honest caveats: gel cooling is gentle and time-limited (it cools for a period, then needs off-time to recharge — it's not the constant deep cold of a frozen pad or AC), and crucially, like all gel mats it is not chew-proof — a determined chewer can puncture it and reach the gel, which (while typically non-toxic) you don't want them ingesting, so it's best for dogs that won't chew it. But for the most convenient, no-power, genuinely-effective everyday cooling for a non-chewing dog, the Green Pet Shop mat is the default.

sections.heading: Best for chewers and the budget pick: K&H Coolin' Pad and Chillz
paragraphs: The K&H Coolin' Pet Pad is the pick for dogs that might chew, because it's a water-filled cooling mat rather than a gel one — and that's a meaningful safety and durability difference. You fill it with water (no electricity needed), and the water draws heat from the dog to cool them, staying cool through evaporation and the thermal mass of the water. The key advantages: water is completely harmless if the mat is somehow punctured (unlike gel, which you don't want a dog ingesting), and K&H's water pads are known for being more durable and puncture-resistant than thin gel mats, making them a safer choice for dogs that chew or scratch at bedding. K&H is a long-trusted pet-bedding brand. The trade-offs: you have to fill it with water (and it's heavier once filled), water cooling is gentle and the mat gradually warms to room temperature (it cools by being cooler than the dog, not by active refrigeration), and it's not bottomlessly chew-proof either — but for a safer, more durable, water-based mat for chewers, it's the standout.

The Chillz Cooling Mat is the budget pick — an affordable, popular pressure-activated gel cooling mat (similar in concept to the Green Pet Shop) at a lower price, for someone who wants self-cooling convenience cheaply. It works the same no-power way: the non-toxic gel activates under the dog's weight to draw away heat, recharging when the dog steps off, with no electricity, water, or refrigeration needed, in various sizes. It's a frequent best-seller precisely because it delivers the convenient gel-cooling experience at a value price. The build and longevity may not quite match the Green Pet Shop, and it shares the same gel-mat caveats (gentle, time-limited cooling; not chew-proof), but for an affordable, effective, no-fuss gel cooling mat, it's the value standout — effectively a cheaper alternative to the Green Pet Shop, worth comparing on current price and size.

Choose between them by your dog. The K&H water pad wins for chewers and durability-and-safety priorities (harmless water, tougher build). The Chillz wins on price for convenient gel cooling cheaply for a non-chewing dog. The K&H is the safer water mat for chewers; the Chillz the budget gel mat.

sections.heading: The self-cooling fabric mat and the value gel pick: Arf Pets and Frisco
paragraphs: The Arf Pets Self-Cooling Mat is another popular pressure-activated gel mat, positioned as a well-reviewed, often mid-priced option with a focus on a durable cover and a range of sizes. Like the Green Pet Shop and Chillz, it self-cools via non-toxic gel that activates under the dog's weight with no power, water, or freezer needed, recharging during off-time. Arf Pets is known for pet products with solid build quality and often includes a sturdier or more scratch-resistant cover than the cheapest mats, plus multiple size options for everything from small dogs to large breeds. It's a strong alternative in the gel-mat category for someone who wants convenient self-cooling with a bit more attention to cover durability, at a reasonable price. It shares the universal gel-mat caveats (gentle time-limited cooling, not chew-proof), but as a well-built, well-sized gel mat, it's a dependable pick.

The Frisco Cooling Mat is the value retailer-brand pick — Frisco (Chewy's house brand) offers affordable, no-nonsense pressure-activated gel cooling mats that do the core self-cooling job dependably at a budget-friendly price, in a range of sizes, with the convenience of a widely-available, well-reviewed house brand. It works the same gel way (no power, no water, recharges off-pressure), and it's a sensible, economical choice for someone who wants a straightforward cooling mat without overthinking the brand. Like all gel mats it's gentle, time-limited, and not chew-proof, and the build is value-tier, but for an affordable, dependable everyday gel cooling mat from a trusted pet retailer, it's a solid budget option alongside the Chillz.

Choose between them by emphasis. The Arf Pets wins for a gel mat with a bit more cover durability and good size range at a reasonable mid-price. The Frisco wins on affordable, dependable house-brand value. Both are convenient no-power gel mats; the Arf Pets leans slightly more durable, the Frisco slightly more budget.

sections.heading: How to choose: cooling type, chew-resistance, size, and safe use
paragraphs: Decide between gel and water cooling, because it affects convenience, safety, and durability. Pressure-activated gel mats (Green Pet Shop, Chillz, Arf Pets, Frisco) are the most convenient — no power, water, or refrigeration; the gel activates under the dog's weight and recharges automatically during off-time — making them effortless to use anywhere (floor, crate, car, bed). Water-filled mats (K&H) require filling with water but offer two advantages: water is completely harmless if punctured (gel, while typically non-toxic, is something you don't want a dog ingesting), and water pads are often more durable and puncture-resistant. Both cool gently by being cooler than the dog rather than actively refrigerating. Choose gel for maximum convenience for a non-chewing dog, or water for a safer, tougher option for a chewer.

Critically, consider chew-resistance and supervise, because the biggest risk with any cooling mat is a dog chewing it. No cooling mat — gel or water — is truly chew-proof, and a determined chewer can puncture one, potentially ingesting gel or just destroying the mat. So: only use a cooling mat with a dog that doesn't chew its bedding, or supervise use and remove the mat when you're not watching; if your dog is a chewer, a water-filled mat (K&H) is the safer choice because water is harmless if released, and a more durable cover helps, but supervision is still essential. Never assume a cooling mat is safe to leave with a chewing dog unattended. Match the mat's durability and type to your dog's chewing tendency, and prioritise safety over convenience for chewers.

Size it to your dog and understand realistic cooling. Choose a mat large enough for your dog to lie on comfortably (most come in multiple sizes from small to extra-large; size up for big breeds or for a dog that likes to sprawl) — too small and the dog won't use it. Set realistic expectations on cooling: these mats provide gentle, passive relief — they're cooler than the floor and draw away some body heat to help an overheating dog feel more comfortable, but they are not air conditioning and won't deeply chill a dog or substitute for proper heat safety (shade, water, avoiding hot cars and midday walks). Gel mats cool for a period then need off-time to recharge; water mats gradually warm to room temperature. Use a cooling mat as one tool for summer comfort — on the floor, in a crate, or in the car — alongside the essentials of fresh water, shade, and avoiding overheating, and choose the type (gel for convenience, water for chewers/safety) and size that fit your dog.

faqs.q: How do dog cooling mats work — do they need electricity or freezing?
faqs.a: The popular ones need neither electricity nor freezing, which is their main appeal. The two main types both cool passively. Pressure-activated gel mats (like the Green Pet Shop, Chillz, Arf Pets, and Frisco) contain a non-toxic cooling gel that activates under the dog's body weight: when the dog lies down, the gel draws heat away from the dog's body, keeping them cooler, and once the dog steps off for a while, the gel automatically re-cools (recharges) on its own — no power, no water, no refrigeration, just lay it down and it works. Water-filled mats (like the K&H) are filled with water, which cools the dog through the thermal mass and evaporation of the water — again no electricity, you just add water. Both types work by being cooler than the dog and absorbing some of its body heat, providing gentle, passive cooling relief. Neither needs to be frozen or plugged in (though you can sometimes pre-chill a gel mat in the fridge for extra effect). This is what makes them convenient to use anywhere — on the floor, in a crate, on a dog bed, or in the car — but it also means the cooling is gentle and time-limited rather than the deep, constant cold of a freezer or air conditioning.

faqs.q: Are dog cooling mats safe if my dog chews?
faqs.a: This is the most important safety consideration, and the honest answer is that no cooling mat is truly chew-proof, so chewing dogs need care. A determined chewer can puncture or tear any cooling mat. With gel mats, puncturing releases the cooling gel — most reputable mats use non-toxic gel, but it's still not something you want your dog ingesting, and a destroyed mat is a waste — so gel mats are best used only with dogs that don't chew their bedding. With water-filled mats (like the K&H), the key safety advantage is that the filling is just water, which is completely harmless if the mat is punctured, and water pads are often built more durably and puncture-resistant — making them the safer choice for dogs that might chew or scratch. Regardless of type, the safe approach for any dog with chewing tendencies is to supervise use and remove the mat when you can't watch, rather than leaving it with the dog unattended. If your dog is a known chewer, choose a durable water-filled mat and still supervise; if your dog reliably doesn't chew its bedding, a convenient gel mat is fine. Never assume a cooling mat is safe to leave unattended with a chewer — it's both a choking/ingestion risk and a destroyed-mat risk.

faqs.q: Do cooling mats actually keep a dog cool, or is it air conditioning?
faqs.a: They provide genuine but gentle, passive relief — they are definitely not air conditioning, and it's important to have realistic expectations. A cooling mat works by being cooler than your dog and absorbing some of its body heat when the dog lies on it, which helps an overheating dog feel more comfortable and offers a cool spot to rest, especially on a hot day or a warm floor. That relief is real and welcome — dogs often seek out and settle on them in summer. But the cooling is mild and limited: gel mats cool for a period and then need off-time to recharge, and water mats gradually warm toward room temperature, so neither delivers the constant, deep cold of a frozen pad, a fan, or air conditioning, and a mat alone won't 'cool down' a seriously overheated dog. Crucially, a cooling mat is not a substitute for proper heat safety: in hot weather your dog still needs constant access to fresh water and shade, avoidance of hot cars (never leave a dog in a parked car in heat) and midday walks on hot pavement, and prompt attention if showing signs of heatstroke (heavy panting, drooling, lethargy, collapse — a veterinary emergency). Use a cooling mat as one helpful comfort tool among proper heat precautions, not as your primary or only way to keep a dog cool.
